promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Edit target: keep the gallery; the pasted boats keep their exact silhouette, size and position

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit Reference 1, a finished 3:2 (1536x1024) story illustration, and change only what is seen through the big window.

Keep EVERYTHING in the gallery exactly as it is, pixel for pixel: the manager and his gesture, Castle and the miners behind the tape, the guards, the families with luggage at the gate, the gangway, the departures panels, the floor, the lights, the camera and the composition. The window's heavy bolted frame and its two vertical mullions stay in front of everything outside; repair them wherever a pasted boat overlaps them.

Through the window, the old freighter is gone. Instead, beyond the glass, a dim pressurized launch bay cut into the asteroid rock, lit by a few hard floodlights, with two small company boats on their landing pads. Repaint the two pasted renders so they belong in the painting, keeping each one's exact silhouette, size, position and angle; do not reshape, enlarge or add parts. They are short, boxy 9-metre shuttles in pale grey and off-white plating with dark window bands at the nose, a small turret on top and a side boarding door; the nearer one has its side door open with light spilling out, and its stubby landing legs stand on the pad. A ground crew figure or two beside them for scale, a fuel hose, pad markings. The boats are plainly too small for everyone in the gallery: two boats, a handful of seats.

Same restrained painted realism, amber and cool light as the rest of the image. No new text.
